chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, Muhammad ibn Isa, Al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim ibn Sufyan, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Your breaking of the fast in the house of your Muslim brother is superior to your fasting seventy times over, or ninety times over.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for hosting a Muslim brother for iftar during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to emphasize that the social act of *iftar* (breaking the fast) with a brother holds greater merit than the individual act of fasting itself, specifically quantified as seventy or ninety times the reward. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on communal solidarity and hospitality (*karam*) as vital components of worship, elevating the spiritual status of strengthening kinship ties (*silat al-rahim*) during the holy month.
